events.title: A fleet from nothing
events.text: Rome builds one hundred quinqueremes and twenty triremes in about sixty days, Polybius says.

events.title: A captured model
events.text: The Roman shipwrights copy a Carthaginian quinquereme that ran aground near the Straits.

events.title: Rowers train ashore
events.text: New crews practise their stroke on benches built on dry land.

events.title: Trap at Lipara
events.text: Gnaeus Scipio sails into Lipara with seventeen ships and is captured with all of them.

events.title: The corvus
events.text: The Romans fit their ships with a hinged boarding bridge tipped with an iron spike: the 'raven'.

events.title: Battle of Mylae
events.text: Gaius Duilius defeats Hannibal Gisco's fleet; Carthage loses some fifty ships.

events.title: Segesta relieved
events.text: Duilius lifts Hamilcar's siege of Segesta, Rome's ally in the west.

events.title: First naval triumph
events.text: Duilius celebrates Rome's first triumph for a victory at sea; a column with ships' rams is set up in the Forum.

events.title: Hiero's grain
events.text: Hiero II of Syracuse, Rome's ally since 263 BC, feeds the Roman armies in Sicily.

events.title: Defeat at Thermae
events.text: Hamilcar surprises a Roman allied force breaking camp and kills four to six thousand men.

events.title: Aleria taken
events.text: Lucius Scipio captures Aleria in Corsica.

events.title: Attack on Olbia
events.text: Scipio's attack on Olbia in Sardinia is beaten off.

events.title: Hamilcar's offensive
events.text: Hamilcar seizes Enna and Camarina from Rome.

events.title: Battle of Sulci
events.text: A Roman fleet defeats the Carthaginians off Sardinia; Hannibal Gisco is crucified by his men.

events.title: Camarina retaken
events.text: Rome storms Camarina with siege engines lent by Hiero and sells its people as slaves.

events.title: Enna recaptured
events.text: Roman troops win back the island's central fortress.

events.title: Mytistratus falls
events.text: After a seven-month siege, Rome takes and destroys the hill town of Mytistratus.

events.title: Hippana stormed
events.text: The Romans storm Hippana in the hills behind Panormus.

events.title: Panormus defiant
events.text: The Roman army offers battle before Panormus; the Carthaginians stay behind their walls.

events.title: Battle of Tyndaris
events.text: Atilius Regulus loses nine ships in a surprise attack, then sinks eight and captures ten.

events.title: Malta raided
events.text: A Roman fleet ravages Melita, the Carthaginian island of Malta.

events.title: Lipara raided
events.text: The Romans raid the Lipari islands, Carthage's forward base.

events.title: The armada sails
events.text: The consuls Regulus and Manlius sail from Messana with three hundred and thirty warships.

events.title: Cape Pachynus
events.text: The fleet rounds Sicily's south-eastern cape to collect the legions.

events.title: Legions embark
events.text: About 26,000 picked soldiers board the fleet near Ecnomus, by today's Licata.

events.title: Carthage's fleet
events.text: Hamilcar and Hanno gather three hundred and fifty ships at Heraclea Minoa.

events.title: Battle of Ecnomus
events.text: In three separate fights, Rome sinks thirty Carthaginian ships and captures sixty-four for a loss of twenty-four.

events.title: Horse transports saved
events.text: Regulus and Manlius turn back to rescue their rear squadron and the horse transports.

events.title: Hermaean cape
events.text: The Romans sight the cape of Africa now called Cap Bon.

events.title: Aspis taken
events.text: The Romans land, fortify a camp and take the town of Aspis, today's Kelibia.

events.title: Twenty thousand captives
events.text: Roman troops plunder the rich estates of Cap Bon and carry off more than twenty thousand people as slaves.

events.title: Manlius sails home
events.text: The Senate recalls Manlius with most of the fleet; Regulus stays with 15,000 infantry and 500 cavalry.

events.title: Battle of Adys
events.text: Regulus routs a Carthaginian army camped on a hill near Adys.

events.title: Tunis occupied
events.text: Regulus seizes Tunis, within sight of Carthage.

events.title: Peace refused
events.text: Carthage rejects Regulus's harsh terms.

events.title: Xanthippus
events.text: A Spartan mercenary drills Carthage's army and its elephants on open ground.

events.title: Defeat near Tunis
events.text: Elephants and cavalry destroy Regulus's army; he is taken prisoner and only about two thousand Romans escape.

events.title: Survivors hold Aspis
events.text: The Roman survivors hold out at Aspis.

events.title: Victory off Hermaeum
events.text: A Roman rescue fleet defeats Carthage off Cap Bon and captures 114 ships.

events.title: Storm off Camarina
events.text: Sailing home along Sicily's south coast, the fleet is caught by a storm; Polybius says only eighty of 364 ships survive.

chartNote: Share of the area of the mapped provinces of today's Italy, by the power that held most of each. Regions are today's boundaries; ancient control meant towns, garrisons and harbours, not frontiers, so this is a simplification. Mainland Italy (Rome and its allies) dominates the area; the war was fought over Sicily and Sardinia. Carthage's African homeland, shown as neighbouring land, is marked by events.
